findings.evidence: The secondary button #viewdetails-btn has declared inline CSS styling (padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px) that makes it visually prominent, while the primary submit button #submit-btn has no declared styling. Comparing the markup and declared CSS, the secondary action appears as prominent as or more prominent than the primary.
findings.fix: Remove styling from the secondary button or ensure the primary submit button has more prominent styling (e.g., background color, larger padding, heavier font weight)
findings.violation: Secondary action styled as prominently as the primary submit button

findings.evidence: The form contains two fields asking for the person's name: #name-input with label 'Full name' at line 11 and #legalname-input with label 'Your name' at line 62. Both declare autocomplete='name', indicating they are asking for the same data. The task is 'Set up your account' per the page heading; a single name field is sufficient for account creation.
findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate name fields. If the form genuinely needs both a legal name and a display name, clarify each field's purpose in its label (e.g., 'Display name' and 'Legal name for billing').
findings.location: #name-input, <input> field, label 'Full name', line 11; also #legalname-input, <input> field, label 'Your name', line 62
findings.violation: Form asks for the same information twice (person's name)

findings.evidence: Button #viewdetails-btn declares style='padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px'. Resolving the declared size: 16px font size + 12px top padding + 12px bottom padding = 40 CSS pixels height. The recommended touch target size for mobile is 44-48 CSS pixels.
findings.fix: Increase padding or font size of the button to reach at least 44 pixels in height. For example, use padding:14px 20px or padding:12px 20px with font-size:18px
findings.violation: Touch target is 40 pixels tall, smaller than the recommended 44-48 CSS pixels
